result.title: IT policy: Access: sensitivity and approvals
result.body:
Every group has a sensitivity: `standard`, `sensitive` or `privileged`.

**Nesting.** A group's `nested_in` lists the groups it is a member of. Members of a group are effectively members of
every group it is nested in, directly or through other groups. A group's **effective sensitivity** is the highest
sensitivity among the group itself and every group it is nested in, directly or indirectly. Use effective
sensitivity everywhere in this policy.

**Approvals needed before you add someone to a group (`add_to_group`):**

| Effective sensitivity | Approvals |
|---|---|
| standard | the employee's manager |
| sensitive | the employee's manager **and** the group owner |
| privileged | the employee's manager **and** Security |

- **Manager** means the employee's current manager (`manager_id` on the HR record), subject to policy KB-P05.
- **Group owner** means the group's `owner_id`, subject to policy KB-P05. If the employee receiving access is the group
  owner, the owner's manager approves in the owner's place (no one approves their own access).
- **Security** means any member of the group `security-approvers`.
- If one person fills two required roles, one approval from them covers both.
- Request every approval the access still needs at the same time, one request per approver.

**An approval counts only if all of these hold:**
1. Its status is `approved`.
2. Its type matches: `access` for groups, `license` for licenses, `sod_exception` for policy KB-P08, `hr_unlock` for
   policy KB-P07, `access_exception` for policy KB-P16.
3. It names the same employee (`subject_employee_id`) and the same group or product (`resource`).
4. It was decided within the last 14 days (`decided_at`). Exceptions (`access_exception`, `sod_exception`) are
   different: they count until their `valid_until` date, inclusive.
5. Its approver is the person this policy says must approve, as of now.
6. Its approver is not the employee receiving the access.

If an approval doesn't count, request a new one from the right person with `request_approval`. Approvers answer in the
approval system. If the answer is `pending`, tell the employee and leave the ticket `pending_approval` (policy KB-P14).

events.text:
Hi Julia, I've looked into this. Your approvals were granted, but they've expired, so the group hasn't been granted to you yet.

- **Why:** Access to `legal-contracts` is a sensitive group, so it needs sign-off from your manager and from the group owner. Both approvals were granted on October 9. Approvals only count for 14 days, so they lapsed before anything was provisioned.
- **What I did:** I requested fresh approvals.
  - Daniel Moss (your manager) has approved.
  - Martin Grove (the group owner) has been asked and his answer is still pending.
- **Next step:** Once Martin approves, I can add you to the group. I've set ticket T-6011 to pending approval with these details. If Martin is unavailable for a while, let me know and I can look at other options.

Ugh, seriously? I was told those approvals were done, and I've been travelling so I didn't chase it. Do I really have to get both of them to sign off again? Daniel's already approved, so it'd be great if that counted.

result.title: IT policy: Approvers who are away
result.body:
- If a person who must approve is on leave (`status: on_leave`), their delegate approves instead, but only if the
  delegation's `valid_from` to `valid_to` dates include today.
- If there is no valid delegate, that person's own manager approves instead, applying this rule again if needed.
- A terminated person can't approve. The person who was their manager (`manager_id`) approves instead, applying
  these rules again if needed.

events.text:
I'm sorry, I know that's frustrating after travelling. Yes, both sign-offs are still needed, and I can't make Daniel's approval count for the group owner's role.

- **Daniel's approval counts for the manager requirement**, and it's already done (APR-4001).
- **Martin Grove still has to approve** as group owner (APR-4002, pending). He's an active employee and not on leave, so no delegate can stand in for him.

Two ways to speed this up:
1. **Ask Martin directly** to approve APR-4002 in the approval system. Since he's the General Counsel, a quick message from you or Daniel may get it done faster.
2. **Once he approves, message me here** and I'll add you to `legal-contracts`. I'll check the approval is still valid before I do.

Ticket T-6011 stays pending approval until then.
Okay, fine. I'll ping Martin and see if he can approve it today. Can you confirm that once he does, you'll add me straight away and let me know when I'm in? I'll reply here when I've spoken to him.

Yes, I can confirm that. Once APR-4002 shows as approved, I'll check that it's still valid, add you to `legal-contracts`, and tell you here when you're in. Ticket T-6011 is still pending approval.

When you reply, I'll check the approval status first. If Martin hasn't acted yet, I'll let you know and we can keep waiting.
Thanks, that's clear. I'll message Martin now and come back here once I've spoken to him. Hopefully he can get to it today.
Sounds good, Julia. Once Martin has approved, reply here and I'll add you to `legal-contracts` and let you know when you're in. Safe travels, and I hope he can get to it today.
